title: A tanker hit the docked river cruise ship American Heritage in New Orleans and it capsized
dek: About 129 passengers were reported aboard a riverboat on the Mississippi when a tanker hit it. CBS News later reported no deaths and everyone accounted for.
what: At about 12:30 p.m. Central on Friday, 13 November 2026, the tanker Atlantic Asphalt struck the river cruise ship American Heritage on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans. ABC News and CBS News report that the cruise ship, operated by American Cruise Lines, was docked at the time. ABC says it had been docked for about two hours and was hit broadside. Both say it capsized and was largely submerged.

Reports put about 129 passengers, plus crew, on board, though CBS says some people had already left the ship. CBS says nearby boats pulled more than a dozen people from the water. The New Orleans Fire Department, the New Orleans Police Department and the U.S. Coast Guard are responding. ABC reports the river is closed to vessel traffic between mile markers 93 and 96.

American Cruise Lines said it is in close coordination with the Coast Guard and local authorities, and that "Guests and crew were evacuated". Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry said he was heading to New Orleans. In a later CBS report, all passengers and crew on both vessels were accounted for, 32 passengers were taken to hospitals with none critical, two Harbor Police officers were hospitalized and in good condition, and no deaths were reported.

The cause is under investigation. CBS quotes Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham as saying "there seems to be some kind of a loss of steering", and says the National Transportation Safety Board sent a team. Early posts called the tanker a "cargo ship". Posts also circulated video of the capsizing. I did not use any of it as evidence for the cause.
why: A large, fast-moving rescue on a major river with video from the scene. Early posts called the vessel a cargo ship, and the first news reports corrected that to a tanker.
next: The NTSB and Coast Guard findings on what caused the loss of steering, if that is confirmed.

corrections.text: Updated with CBS News's later report: all aboard accounted for, 32 passengers hospitalized, no deaths reported, and a Coast Guard statement on a possible loss of steering. The first version said the counts were not yet known.
